title: Beechcraft Bonanza V35B — Emergency Procedures
description: Emergency procedures for the Beechcraft Bonanza V35B with Continental IO-520 fuel-injected engine and retractable tricycle gear. Items marked as memory items must be performed from memory before consulting this checklist. All numerical values (airspeeds, altitudes, fuel quantities, power settings) must come from the specific aircraft POH. The V-tail ruddervator arrangement does not change the fundamental emergency priorities but may affect control feel during abnormal situations. Not a substitute for recurrent training, emergency simulation, or type-specific instruction.

source.notes: No manufacturer document consulted. Written from general familiarity with the type.

known_issues.description: Contains no airspeeds, power settings, fuel quantities, or other numerical limitations — all must come from the specific aircraft POH.
Equipment, avionics, and fuel system configurations vary across V35B airframes. Verify every item against the specific aircraft and its POH before use.
This file covers selected emergency scenarios; the aircraft POH contains the authoritative and complete emergency procedure set.

rights.notes: Manufacturer POH remains under copyright. This file does not reproduce its wording or selection of items.

sections.title: Engine Failure on Takeoff — Before or At Liftoff
sections.condition: Engine fails or loses power during takeoff roll or at the moment of liftoff

items.text: Throttle
Brakes — apply firmly to stop on remaining runway
Mixture
Ignition
Master switch
Do not attempt to continue the takeoff after an engine failure below a safe maneuvering altitude. A straight-ahead landing or controlled stop is nearly always the correct choice.

sections.title: Engine Failure After Takeoff — Low Altitude
sections.condition: Engine fails or loses significant power after liftoff at low altitude

items.text: Pitch — lower nose immediately to maintain airspeed above stall
items.response: PITCH FOR BEST GLIDE OR Vx PER POH; DO NOT STALL

items.text: Landing area — select straight-ahead or slight turn only
items.response: BEST AVAILABLE AREA SELECTED; AVOID STEEP TURNS

items.text: Throttle
Mixture
Fuel selector
Landing gear — extend if landing is committed and runway is ahead
items.response: GEAR DOWN IF SUITABLE SURFACE AVAILABLE; GEAR UP FOR SOFT-FIELD FORCED LANDING

items.text: At low altitude, time is the critical factor. Fly the aircraft first. Checklist use is secondary to maintaining airspeed and establishing a landing attitude.

sections.title: Engine Failure in Flight — Altitude Available
sections.condition: Complete or partial engine power loss at altitude with time to troubleshoot

items.text: Airspeed — establish best glide speed per POH immediately
items.response: BEST GLIDE SPEED ESTABLISHED PER POH

items.text: Landing area — identify and begin planning approach
Throttle
Mixture
Fuel selector
Ignition switch
Primer (if equipped)
Throttle — attempt restart with starter if altitude permits
items.response: STARTER ENGAGED; MIXTURE ADVANCED AS ENGINE FIRES

items.text: If restart unsuccessful — declare emergency
items.response: SQUAWK 7700; ADVISE ATC OF POSITION AND INTENTIONS

items.text: If restart unsuccessful — proceed to Forced Landing checklist

sections.title: Engine Fire in Flight
sections.condition: Fire visible at engine or firewall, or smoke entering cockpit from engine area

items.text: Mixture
Fuel selector
Throttle
items.response: FULL OPEN — TO EXHAUST FUEL IN LINES

items.text: Master switch
Cabin heat and air vents
Airspeed — increase to POH-specified diving speed to blow out fire if appropriate
items.response: AIRSPEED INCREASED PER POH; SIDESLIP AWAY FROM FIRE

items.text: Emergency descent — begin immediately toward nearest suitable landing area
Land as soon as possible — proceed to Forced Landing checklist
items.response: NEAREST SUITABLE AREA SELECTED; FORCED LANDING INITIATED

items.text: An engine fire is an immediate threat. Land as soon as possible. Do not delay to troubleshoot or restart.

sections.title: Engine Fire on the Ground
sections.condition: Fire at engine during start or ground operation

items.text: Throttle — continue cranking to draw fire back into engine if fire during start
items.response: CRANKING WITH THROTTLE OPEN AND MIXTURE RICH TO CLEAR FUEL

items.text: If fire persists — mixture to idle cutoff
Ignition switch
Master switch
Fuel selector
Evacuate aircraft — all occupants exit and move upwind
Fire extinguisher — use ground extinguisher on cowling if safe to approach
items.response: EXTINGUISHER APPLIED OR EMERGENCY SERVICES CALLED

items.text: Emergency services — call 911 or airport fire department

sections.title: Electrical Fire / Smoke in Cockpit
sections.condition: Smoke, burning smell, or visible electrical fire in cockpit or cabin

items.text: Master switch
Avionics master
All electrical switches
Cabin vents and windows — open to ventilate smoke if safe to do so
Fire extinguisher — use dry chemical on source if accessible
If fire extinguished — restore minimum electrical power one switch at a time to identify source
Land as soon as possible — squawk 7700; advise ATC
If smoke or fire recurs when electrical power is restored, turn master back off and maintain VMC navigation using standby instruments.

sections.title: Loss of Oil Pressure
sections.condition: Oil pressure drops below the minimum green arc limit or falls to zero

items.text: Oil pressure gauge — confirm reading and cross-check oil temperature
items.response: LOW PRESSURE CONFIRMED; OIL TEMPERATURE TREND NOTED

items.text: Power — reduce to minimum required for level flight
items.response: POWER REDUCED TO MINIMUM; MONITORING ENGINE

items.text: Land as soon as possible — begin planning immediate descent to nearest suitable airport
ATC — declare emergency, advise position and intentions
If oil pressure falls to zero — treat as imminent engine failure; establish best glide
items.response: BEST GLIDE AIRSPEED ESTABLISHED PER POH

items.text: Low oil pressure with rising oil temperature indicates serious lubrication failure. The IO-520 will seize rapidly without oil pressure. Do not delay in landing or initiating a forced landing procedure.

sections.title: Forced Landing — Power Off
sections.condition: Engine has failed or must be shut down; landing must be made without engine power

items.text: Airspeed — best glide per POH
items.response: BEST GLIDE ESTABLISHED; MAINTAIN UNTIL SHORT FINAL

items.text: Landing area — select field considering wind, obstacles, and surface
items.response: FIELD SELECTED; INTO-WIND OR SLIGHT CROSSWIND ACCEPTABLE

items.text: Squawk 7700 and advise ATC of position
Mixture
Fuel selector
Ignition switch
Master switch — leave ON until flare to retain flaps and gear
Landing gear — extend when landing is assured and field surface is suitable
items.response: GEAR DOWN FOR HARD OR FIRM SURFACE; CONSIDER GEAR UP FOR SOFT FIELD OR WATER

items.text: Flaps — extend as needed to control glide path
items.response: FLAPS EXTENDED AS APPROPRIATE FOR APPROACH

items.text: Seat belts and shoulder harnesses
Master switch — OFF just before touchdown
Doors — unlatch before touchdown to prevent jamming
If landing on a prepared surface gear-down, leave the gear selector DOWN. If landing gear-up on rough terrain or water, confirm gear selector is UP before touchdown.

sections.title: Gear Unsafe / Gear Failure to Extend
sections.condition: Gear-unsafe light illuminates, or one or more green lights fail to appear after gear-down selection

items.text: Airspeed — slow to below gear operating speed per POH
Gear selector — cycle UP then DOWN
Gear position indicator — check all three lights
items.response: LIGHTS CHECKED; IDENTIFY WHICH GEAR IS UNSAFE

items.text: Circuit breakers — check gear-related circuit breakers
items.response: BREAKERS CHECKED; RESET IF POPPED (ONCE ONLY)

items.text: Gear-unsafe light — verify it is not a bulb failure by pressing press-to-test
If gear fails to extend normally — proceed to emergency gear extension procedure
If gear remains unsafe after emergency extension — advise ATC; plan minimum-damage gear-up landing
items.response: ATC ADVISED; GEAR-UP LANDING PLANNED PER POH GUIDANCE

sections.title: Emergency Gear Extension
sections.condition: Normal hydraulic gear extension has failed; manual emergency extension required

items.text: Emergency gear extension procedure for the V35B uses a manual hand pump or free-fall mechanism depending on system configuration. Refer to the specific aircraft POH for the correct procedure — the following is a generic framework only.
Airspeed — reduce to below emergency gear extension speed per POH
items.response: AIRSPEED AT OR BELOW LIMIT PER POH

items.text: Gear selector — place in DOWN position
Emergency gear release or hand pump — locate and activate per POH
items.response: EMERGENCY RELEASE ACTIVATED OR HAND PUMP OPERATED PER POH

items.text: Gear position indicator — check for three green after emergency extension
items.response: THREE GREEN CONFIRMED OR NOT — NOTE RESULT

items.text: Fly-by or tower visual check if any doubt about gear position
items.response: TOWER OR AIRCRAFT VISUAL CONFIRMATION OBTAINED

items.text: If gear cannot be confirmed down — plan landing with emergency services standing by
items.response: EMERGENCY SERVICES REQUESTED; LANDING APPROACH PLANNED

items.text: Land with minimum side load; avoid hard landing to prevent gear collapse
